thread_analysis.thread_summary: This is the earliest historical capture of the Topre Corporation R4H/RC1 keyboard certification saga (contacts Kenki Enomoto, Seiji Hiraki, Takato Kamei, with Allion's Toshitaka Mochizuki, Misumi Sato, Itsuo Sakai), already extensively documented in thread_0211, thread_0224, and thread_0267 for its HOGP/BAS/DIS/HIDS Bluetooth PTS debugging content. This thread's earliest portion additionally covers the combined WHQL/USB side of the engagement (USB IOP+Chapter9 testing, sample shipment, a JP-keyboard USB Fail requiring firmware update and retest, file-download password troubleshooting) and two genuinely new, distinct questions: whether adding a new HID keycode requires re-registration, and whether battery-charging current draw needs special USB test documentation.
all_questions_found: Does adding a new keycode (e.g., Mute) to an already-certified keyboard require re-registration? (see thread_0001_case_01)
Does variable battery-charging current draw require additional USB IOP/Chapter 9 documentation? (see thread_0001_case_02)

(Already documented in thread_0211's case files) HOGP/BAS/DIS/HIDS PTS debugging, Nordic QDID:44613 Profile Subsystem fallback, and related Bluetooth-specific technical content from this same keyboard project.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Beyond the duplicated Bluetooth-specific PTS debugging content (see thread_0211 for the full record), this thread's new contributions clarify that incremental HID keycode additions don't require re-registration unless accompanied by a new model name, and that battery-charging current draw variability falls outside USB IOP/Chapter 9's regulated scope.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0001_case_01 and thread_0001_case_02 for the new decision logic; the duplicated Bluetooth PTS content follows the logic already documented in thread_0211.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified in the newly-extracted content.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: This thread reinforces thread_0211's findings for the same Topre keyboard project and adds two practical post-certification/pre-test scoping lessons: incremental keycode additions don't require re-registration absent a new model name, and battery-related current draw variability doesn't require special USB test documentation.
